Wildfire smoke has a different composition—more sooty black carbon than sulfates, for instance—so the consequences for weather and climate are not as well understood. Smoke this high in the atmosphere also may have effects on the chemistry of stratospheric ozone . Smoke that reaches the stratosphere generally stays there for several months, traveling thousands of kilometers from its source.
